\chapter{Writing --- Your Own Line}
\label{ch:ge-eigene-zeile}
\hlchaptermodality{53}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can write one line about myself from a closed supply of known words, with nothing to copy, and capitalise every noun.}

Complete GE-W02-eigene-zeile: a greeting and a name chosen rather than copied, with the capitals checked before anything else.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[(eigene Zeile)]{Your own line — the first writing with no model}

\label{lesson:GE-W02-eigene-zeile}



\begin{quote}
You have written \textbf{Hallo} four ways: traced, copied, copied from memory, and written from the sound alone.

Every one of those had something to reach for. This one does not.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — controlled composition}
Write \textbf{one line} about yourself: a greeting, then your name.

Nothing is supplied. You choose the words, and the supply you are choosing from is closed — only what this book has taught you.

Before you write, one thing to decide deliberately rather than by accident: \textbf{which nouns get a capital?} In German the answer is \emph{all of them}, not only the ones that name a person or a place. Your line will have at least one, and an English-trained hand will lower-case it without noticing.

Write the line. Then read it back and check the capitals \textbf{before} you check anything else.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which German nouns take a capital letter? (\textbf{All of them.})

And what did you have to choose, that the last four lessons chose for you? (\textbf{The words.})
\end{tcolorbox}
